items.subject: english
items.derivation: Paragraph 1 expressly describes notifications interrupting conversations and attracting attention to screens.

decisive_support.quote: Notifications repeatedly interrupt conversations and draw fingers towards screens.

option_claims.text: Repeatedly draw their attention away from conversations
option_claims.assessment: Directly restates both effects in the passage.

option_claims.text: Help them listen more closely to others
option_claims.assessment: Closer listening contradicts interrupted conversations.

option_claims.text: Make their time pass more slowly
option_claims.assessment: No slowing of time is claimed.

option_claims.text: Prevent them from looking at screens
option_claims.assessment: Attention is drawn towards screens, not prevented from reaching them.

items.subject: english
items.derivation: Drifting autumn leaves represent passing, fleeting moments. The surrounding sentences place attention on notifications and screens.

decisive_support.quote: Moments drift away like autumn leaves in the wind. Notifications repeatedly interrupt conversations and draw fingers towards screens.

option_claims.text: Time remains fixed while people use their phones
option_claims.assessment: Fixed time contradicts moments drifting away.

option_claims.text: Moments pass fleetingly while attention is elsewhere
option_claims.assessment: Combines the fleeting-time metaphor with the stated diverted attention.

option_claims.text: Notifications follow a carefully controlled seasonal schedule
option_claims.assessment: The passage does not describe a seasonal notification schedule.

option_claims.text: People deliberately preserve every passing moment
option_claims.assessment: It describes moments slipping away, not deliberately preserving them.

items.subject: english
items.derivation: Anxiety and incompleteness when the device is absent establish psychological dependence. The absent-limb comparison is explicitly figurative.

decisive_support.quote: When phones are out of reach, people feel anxious and incomplete. The writer compares this feeling to a phantom limb: an absent digital device seems like a missing part of oneself. Fear of missing out drives repeated checking.

option_claims.text: Psychological dependence on technology for a sense of completeness
option_claims.assessment: Restates the anxiety and incomplete-self concern.

option_claims.text: Physical damage to arms caused by holding a phone
option_claims.assessment: No arm injury is described.

option_claims.text: The expense of replacing lost digital devices
option_claims.assessment: Replacement expense is absent from the passage.

option_claims.text: An inability to read the time without a smartwatch
option_claims.assessment: Neither a smartwatch nor inability to read time is mentioned.

items.subject: english
items.derivation: The question asks for an inference about device-free hours, not a clinical cure. Among these alternatives, reducing repeated update checking addresses the stated compulsion; the other outcomes are unsupported guarantees or unrelated claims.

decisive_support.quote: When phones are out of reach, people feel anxious and incomplete. The writer compares this feeling to a phantom limb: an absent digital device seems like a missing part of oneself. Fear of missing out drives repeated checking.

option_claims.text: Reducing the compulsion to keep checking updates
option_claims.assessment: Addresses the repeated-checking behaviour named in paragraph 2.

option_claims.text: Guaranteeing that no important message ever arrives
option_claims.assessment: Device-free hours cannot guarantee that no message arrives.

option_claims.text: Increasing the number of likes on every post
option_claims.assessment: The passage supplies no mechanism or promise of more likes.

option_claims.text: Removing the need for any human conversation
option_claims.assessment: The passage values human connection and does not remove its need.

items.note: This is an inference item. Separate CUET-fit review must judge the strength of the inference and distractors.

items.subject: english
items.derivation: Paragraph 3 connects dissonance with unheard life rhythm and information overload. Alternatives A, B and C can all describe that disruption. No decisive textual distinction makes exactly one of those interpretations correct.

decisive_support.quote: Thumbs move like skilled pianists, but the true rhythm of life remains unheard amid the dissonance of digital noise. Constant connectivity creates a hunch on shoulders, a physical sign of the burden of information overload. Minds stay alert for the next like, share or comment.

option_claims.text: It creates a jarring and chaotic environment that disrupts focus.
option_claims.assessment: A jarring environment disrupting focus is defensible.

option_claims.text: It contributes to a sense of overload, overwhelming the senses.
option_claims.assessment: Overload is explicitly mentioned and is defensible.

option_claims.text: It interferes with engagement in meaningful aspects of life.
option_claims.assessment: Interference with meaningful life is supported by the unheard rhythm and paragraph 4.

option_claims.text: It induces stress by interrupting with regular updates about the device.
option_claims.assessment: Regular updates about the device itself are not established.

items.subject: english
items.derivation: A hunch is explicitly labelled a physical sign, but thumb movement is also a bodily sign of digital engagement. The current question asks about engagement, rather than the bodily burden alone. The phrase most directly does not establish an exclusive condition.

decisive_support.quote: Thumbs move like skilled pianists, but the true rhythm of life remains unheard amid the dissonance of digital noise. Constant connectivity creates a hunch on shoulders, a physical sign of the burden of information overload. Minds stay alert for the next like, share or comment.

option_claims.text: Thumbs moving like skilled pianists
option_claims.assessment: Thumb movement is a bodily behaviour associated with engagement.

option_claims.text: Waiting for another like or comment
option_claims.assessment: Waiting for a like is a mental anticipation, not a bodily sign.

option_claims.text: A hunch on shoulders caused by the burden of connectivity
option_claims.assessment: The hunch is expressly described as a physical sign.

option_claims.text: The true rhythm of life remaining unheard
option_claims.assessment: The unheard rhythm is figurative, not an anatomical sign.

items.subject: english
items.derivation: The contrast between digital activity and an unheard life rhythm is developed in paragraph 4 through fleeting genuine connections and sacrificed shared experiences.

decisive_support.quote:
Thumbs move like skilled pianists, but the true rhythm of life remains unheard amid the dissonance of digital noise. Constant connectivity creates a hunch on shoulders, a physical sign of the burden of information overload. Minds stay alert for the next like, share or comment.

(4) Despite efforts to stay connected, people become increasingly isolated among digital faces. Genuine connections are fleeting amid the constant clamour for attention. The search for digital validation sacrifices meaningful moments and shared experiences.

option_claims.text: Meaningful human connections and lived experiences
option_claims.assessment: Fits the connection and lived-experience contrast developed in paragraphs 3–4.

option_claims.text: The speed at which thumbs type messages
option_claims.assessment: Typing speed is part of the digital activity contrasted with the rhythm.

option_claims.text: The mechanical vibration of a phone
option_claims.assessment: No mechanical vibration is identified as the rhythm.

option_claims.text: The count of likes and shares on a screen
option_claims.assessment: Likes and shares are digital validation, contrasted with meaningful experiences.

items.subject: english
items.derivation: The relation is an action or sound to its manner: a whisper is quiet and a clamour is loud. Clamour is the passage word denoting loud noise or demand.

decisive_support.quote: Genuine connections are fleeting amid the constant clamour for attention. The search for digital validation sacrifices meaningful moments and shared experiences.

option_claims.text: validation
option_claims.assessment: Validation is approval, not a loud sound.

option_claims.text: fleeting
option_claims.assessment: Fleeting denotes brief duration.

option_claims.text: essence
option_claims.assessment: Essence denotes a fundamental quality.

option_claims.text: clamour
option_claims.assessment: Clamour supplies the loud-sound side of the analogy.

items.note: The ordinary lexical interpretation is independently derived from the passage usage; the official key has not been read.
